title: Pay station and kiosk UI
idea: The parking frontend is a few kiosk screens; the pay station runs on one reducer and one Idempotency-Key per amount, so retries never double-charge.
points: KioskApp holds the pay reducer; PayStation renders it and dispatches.
The pay request fires once per PAYING step; extra taps are ignored.
One Idempotency-Key per quoted amount survives retries, so a retry never double-charges.
Follow-ups: plate cameras instead of tickets, many lots, and live free-spot boards.

hero.title: Screens to database, end to end

edges.caption: Gate kiosks run one screen each: entry posts the plate and prints a ticket; exit shows Please pay on 409.
KioskApp holds the pay reducer and passes state and dispatch down to PayStation.
In IDLE it shows ScanPrompt. A scan dispatches SCANNED and the step becomes QUOTING.
After QUOTE_OK it shows FeeQuote with the server's amount, never a browser guess.

edges.label: pay
edges.caption: PAY_CLICKED creates the key once. One effect sends POST /tickets/:id/payments with it.
POST /tickets/:id/payments carries the Idempotency-Key; the controller validates with zod.
One transaction checks the key, marks the ticket PAID and inserts the payment.

code.title: Pay station reducer
code.caption: Pure screen logic. Run it, then add a DRIVER_LEFT event before the last SCANNED and predict the final line.

walk.text: The whole screen state: step, ticket, quoted amount, Idempotency-Key and error.
A scan starts a quote only from IDLE; a failed quote returns to IDLE.
A new amount drops the old key: it is a different payment request.
When a new billed hour starts, the quote is fetched again.
Pay works only from QUOTED and makes the key once, so double taps change nothing.
A failed payment returns to QUOTED but keeps the key for the retry.
The run: a double tap, two failures, a new hour, then success.

code.title: PayStation component
code.caption: A React component that renders state and runs one effect per step. Not run here.

walk.text: Props bring the reducer state, dispatch and the API client.
Entering QUOTING fetches the fee once and reports success or failure.
Entering PAYING sends one payment with the key from the reducer.
Each step has its own screen: scan, loading, or paid.
Errors render in an alert region; the button is disabled while paying.

pitfalls: A disabled button is not enough; the reducer and the Idempotency-Key must stop repeats.
Never compute the fee in the browser; show the server's quote and re-quote hourly.
Interview follow-up: for many lots, add `lot_id` to every table and route.

quiz.q: In the run, which key does the final PAY_CLICKED use?
quiz.why: QUOTE_OK with 20000 differs from 15000, so the reducer drops pk-1. PAY_CLICKED then makes the next key, pk-2. Retries before that reused pk-1.

takeaway: One reducer per screen; one key per payment makes retries safe.
